destructive_changes.reason: Deliberate hardening, not data loss: the unnamed on-delete-cascade FK from journal_legs to journal_entries is dropped and immediately re-created as a plain NO ACTION FK in the same transaction, so an entry delete can no longer vaporize legs. No column or data is removed.

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS immediately before each CREATE TRIGGER is the ledger set's reapply-idempotence idiom (drift policy: reapply), mirroring V_ledger_027. Nothing existing is removed on first apply.
The lexical TRUNCATE match is the migration's own BEFORE TRUNCATE guard trigger - the statement that REJECTS truncation of the journal tables. The migration truncates nothing.
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS immediately before each CREATE TRIGGER is the ledger set's reapply-idempotence idiom (drift policy: reapply), matching V030. Nothing existing is removed on first apply.
The lexical TRUNCATE match is the migration's own BEFORE TRUNCATE guard trigger, which rejects truncation of the journal integrity tables. The migration truncates nothing.

The migration drops only the superseded raw-value unique index and normalized non-unique index after its deterministic collision preflight succeeds, then immediately creates the normalized unique index. No table data or identifier history is removed.

The lexical TRUNCATE match is a BEFORE TRUNCATE guard trigger that rejects deletion of immutable tenant-backfill receipts. This migration truncates no data; PostgreSQL regression coverage attempts truncation and verifies refusal with the receipt retained.

Requires human schema/storage and release-operations review. Replaces only security_raw_prices_pkey (security_id, source_id) with (security_id, source_id, price_as_of) so earlier observations remain retained; no row or column is removed. PostgresMigrationRunner executes the constraint replacement and migration-ledger append under one transaction and advisory migration lock, so failed DDL restores the original primary key. Drain legacy price writers before rollout because their old ON CONFLICT target is no longer valid. After multiple dated observations exist, prefer a forward fix; do not restore the old key by deleting history. Any reverse migration requires separately reviewed preservation of every retained observation and proof that the old uniqueness can be restored safely.

Constraint widening, not data loss: ck_tax_lot_mutations_kind, ck_tax_lot_mutations_quantities, and ck_tax_lot_mutations_cost are dropped and immediately re-created in the same transaction as strict supersets that admit the governed AverageCost BasisRedistribution mutation kind and pooled relief basis. Every existing row still satisfies the re-created checks, and no column or data is removed.

Requires human schema/storage review. Replaces only four check constraints transactionally with strict supersets admitting basis-only Amortization. Existing acquisition, disposal and average-cost rules remain intact; every previously valid row stays valid. No table, column, row or acquisition fact is removed. The migration runner rolls back the constraint replacement on failure. Validate fresh and upgrade databases before release.

Requires human schema/storage review. The cost check is dropped and immediately recreated transactionally as a superset: canonical discrete disposals retain current basis in their pre-relief acquisition and governed-adjustment snapshot, while acquisition-cost, AverageCost and PR #3048 amortization cases remain admitted. No columns or data are removed. Follows PR #3048's ordinal 040 amortization migration.

Requires human schema/storage review. Replaces only named check constraints transactionally with supersets admitting governed CorporateAction predecessor closeout and successor opening. Existing acquisition, disposal, redistribution and amortization rules remain valid; no table, column, row or acquisition fact is removed. The new nullable instruction is required only for new successor batches, preserving historical replay. AtomicTaxLotSuccessorMigrationTests exercises a populated through-041 upgrade, preserves legacy row values and migration receipts, reapplies 042 after successor rows exist, and recreates the migration runner on restart. Its injected DDL failure verifies restoration of the prior constraints, absence of the new column and unchanged receipts before retry. This rollback evidence covers an unsuccessful upgrade transaction; it does not authorize a downgrade that removes retained successor instructions.

Requires independent human schema/storage review. Transactionally replaces four existing named CHECK constraints with supersets admitting a basis-only CapitalReturn and replaces the new instruction constraint on explicit reapply. No table, column, row, acquisition fact or historical instruction is removed. The nullable capital_return_instruction is required only for new CapitalReturn batches. Populated through-043 upgrade, retained history, explicit reapply/restart and injected post-drop DDL failure tests are included; hosted PostgreSQL execution is required before release. This permits failed-upgrade rollback, not a downgrade that discards retained capital-return instructions.

Requires independent human schema/storage review. DROP INDEX IF EXISTS immediately precedes CREATE INDEX for the same three tax_lots/tax_lot_policies index names in one transaction, replacing coalesce(financial_account_id, '') with lower(coalesce(financial_account_id, '')) so storage uniqueness and lookups agree with LedgerAccount's case-insensitive FinancialAccountId equality. No table, column, row or value is removed or rewritten; a leading DO block raises before any DDL when retained rows already collide under the case-insensitive key, naming the conflicting group and row counts for operator resolution. Follows the ledger set's drop/recreate reapply idiom (drift policy: reapply). Hosted PostgreSQL execution of the duplicate-label, cross-case lookup and populated pre-check tests is required before release.

Requires human schema/storage review. Replaces only security_governance_events_stream_check with a wider check that keeps every existing stream ('OperatorOverrides', 'Aliases', 'ProjectionRebuild') and admits 'UnderlyingGraph', so declared underlying-graph links can be recorded in the append-only governance log. No row, column or trigger is removed, and the drop and re-add run in the migration runner's single transaction, so a failure leaves the original constraint in place. A reverse migration must not narrow the check while 'UnderlyingGraph' rows exist.
